criteria.text: ADR 0026 records the default class order, the explicit reviewer order that governs it, and the out-of-scope rules of the delivery commitment.
The roadmap-delivery-commitment spec folder and its review record are retired through a spec-retire landing.
A plan that binds a deliverable to an outcome with sources refuses an empty obligation list, or the completion landing refuses a completion that records no delivery fact.
A plan that settles or removes a deliverable succeeds when that deliverable is absent on main.
The plan identity sorts its policy sources in one canonical order.

bench commit and a bench worktree land with --spec admit an unbound change that carries one tickets-only folder with exactly one ticket, when every production path stays inside that ticket's Writes line.
A light-path change still cannot change the commitment policy or a pinned roadmap row, and a spec-less landing of it refuses with the --spec route.

The operating guide and the drain dispatch each kept light-path fix to a fresh write delegate, whatever the active commitment is, and ADR 0028 records that the commitment gates spec implementations only.
Before the first review charge, the spec stage traces each pin row operator, each unexported entry read, and each derived expectation to its grader.
A spec that consolidates repeated rules maps each changed old-rule and new-rule cell to an acceptance row, a flagged addition, or a Won't handle line.
Before the first review charge, the spec author checks every quantified obligation at each affected site and across all tickets.
The caller sweep runs bench consumers for each changed function, including unexported functions.
For each new workflow step, the spec author traces every write through the digests that later checkpoints compare.
bench test reports a tests_run count for each package, and a named check that runs no test fails with a named rule.
bench test prints one failures row for each diagnostic line, and the default mode states the hidden line count.
bench test --checks lists the check inventory, and bench test --check <name> --fixtures lists the fixture family of that check.
bench test --changed names the cause of each selected package, and the unknown-check refusal names the executable that it consulted.

bench gate --checkpoint <spec> --complete grades the tree that the landing publishes, composed through the landing's own delivery-closure transform, so a red that the closure creates refuses the checkpoint.
Every refusal of a write verb renders through one refusal-route registry, and each face declares a typed route and its agent or reviewer authority.
A conformance check proves that every agent route passes the wired guards and that each producing fixture follows its route out of the refused face.
A gate check refuses production code that re-implements slices.Contains, slices.ContainsFunc, a maps.Copy loop, min, max, strings.Cut, strings.CutPrefix, or strings.CutSuffix.
No production site in the kept categories remains when the gate turns the check on.

The ticket checkpoint refuses a commit whose checks omit root conformance, the tests of a package that the ticket Writes line derives, or the whole cmd/bench package when a public response or embed pattern changed.
The ticket checkpoint refuses a planned citation for a row that the committed ticket covers.
bench record chunk refuses a chunk write whose plan digest differs from the record plan digest, and each checkpoint refusal of a record entry names the bench record form that repairs it.
A native bench record assignment form writes the dispatch history of a version 2 completion plan, so no author or orchestrator writes that history as hand-built JSON.
The verification record imports a probe result through its producer owner and keeps the mutated test run exit code apart from the probe command exit code.
PlanLifecycle is the single owner of the managed lifecycle decision, and link, setup, upgrade execution, and unlink consume its complete decision.
Command behavior, reports, validation order, and the transaction owner stay unchanged, and the effect-only Operations view derives from the complete decision.
The implement-spec guidance states that a build does not fold main into its branch in the middle of a chunk.
The implement-spec guidance states that a build dispatches no light-path fix while the build runs.

Before the first edit, the ticket author lists every place the change must reach: callers, tests, fixtures, and exports, and code that the author moves or merges keeps its error handling and validation.
The author charge keeps the witness cap and runs the witnesses through one bench test call with a repeated --package flag.
The ticket author records its own chunk entry and its verification entries.
The review axes of a round run in parallel, and their findings go to one combined repair charge.
A confirming round examines only the findings that it names.
The build log records each reviewer direction that saves a step.
The implement phase runs a chunk checkpoint gate only before a successor chunk.
The final chunk of a build goes straight to final reconciliation and closes through the complete checkpoint alone.
The delivery leaves FT379 and FT369 open.
When MERGE_HEAD exists, bench commit records the merge parent as the second parent of the commit.
bench commit never authors a one-parent commit while merge state is pending.
The delivery closes no roadmap row, and the candidate-set forms --changed, --dry-run --changed, and --ticket stay on FT258.
A spec-stage close lands its staged spec and its deliverable binding on main before the handoff, and the handoff names the binding state.
bench status prints the complete bench commitment start command, with the deliverable that the spec's Roadmap line and path derive.
A ticket Writes line owns .bench/commitment.json, so the build preflight stays green after the binding.

bench worktree land holds one lease in the intent ledger, keyed by the destination branch, from composition through publish, and a second landing on the same destination refuses with the owner's assignment id and a route that waits.
While a chunked build is open, bench worktree land refuses a landing that is not that build's own landing outside a recorded chunk gap, and the refusal names the build and the gap to wait for.
The open-build window opens at bench commitment start and closes on completion, on bench commitment block, or on abandon.
Only a recorded reviewer-owned override with a reason lets a landing move main after the last chunk's freeze, and an agent cannot grant that override to itself.
A record form accepts a fold-delta review in which only conflict-resolved hunks get review, and the final checks include the packages of the merged test files.
A refusal for a moved destination names bench worktree merge and the landing rerun, not bench doctor.

The internal/durablefile leaf replaces one regular file through an adjacent temporary file, synchronizes the file before the rename and the parent directory after it, and reports a failure after the rename with the statement that new bytes may already be visible.
The review-record writer replaces its file through the internal/durablefile leaf, so it synchronizes the parent directory and returns an injected directory-sync failure.
The delivery closes no roadmap row, and FT354 stays open for its other outcomes.
Every remaining classified replacement caller replaces its file through the internal/durablefile leaf, and no migrated caller keeps its own temporary-file, synchronization, and rename sequence.
Each migrated caller keeps its payload, mode, validation, destination authority, sentinel translation, and recovery policy, and each caller failure has a witness.
The delivery closes no roadmap row, and FT354 stays open for its other outcomes.
bench probe takes --with-file, --insert-before, --occurrence, --delete, and repeated --swap and --omit edits that make one combined mutant.
bench probe accepts the prose check and the system suite as targets through the registered check owner.

The verdict row names the first failing test, --expect requires a named witness, a mutant that does not compile reads build-failed with its first build line, and a second probe on the same subject refuses while the first runs.
The delivery closes no roadmap row, and the batch, multi-package, canary, and failing-name faces stay on FT168.
One bench probe call grades several mutants against one shared baseline run and one private build.
One bench probe call grades several packages in one private build.
The spec stage of this slice decides how bench record imports a batch probe result, and FT318 owns that record form.
The delivery closes no roadmap row, and the canary and failing-name faces stay on FT168.
The reviewer can select a map-only route for a ready compiled map, and the full route stays the default.
The route accepts only a ready compiled map with no bench maps diagnostic, and it returns to the reviewer when the map is not spec-grade.
One fresh slicer writes the stories, coverage rows, tickets, and gap log, and the coordinator completes a thin spec that /bench-implement-spec accepts.
A record-only correction that changes a disposition consumes no repair cycle.

The review record has an evidence-only confirmation form that a biting coordinator probe satisfies, and the chunk checkpoint accepts that form in place of three fresh axes for a test-only repair delta.
A test-only repair whose coordinator probe bites closes through the evidence-only confirmation form and needs no confirming round.

bench record ticket <slug> --chunk <id> --ticket <basename> writes the plan amendment when the digest moved, the chunk freeze for the last ticket (FT445 extends the refreeze to any ticket's record call), and one verification entry for each owed requirement in one record write.
bench record excerpt stages the retained last response of the worktree as the excerpt of one planned requirement.
The ticket form composes the shipped amendment, chunk, and verification writer rules with no second copy of a rule.
bench preflight evidence --check-current binds beside a dirty review record of its spec and reports dirty_record.
bench preflight derives one closure proposal that names each required ownership path of a ticket with its source and its reason, and the proposal grants no approval, write, or dispatch authority.
A fence expansion amends the approved spec fence and the ticket Writes line together, and the review preflight grades the spec fence.
Preflight names each caller outside the ticket fence of a changed unexported helper, including the callers from before a move.
A deleted file's Writes entry carries a deletion marker that the preflight accepts.
Before a charge, preflight verifies each supported spec premise against one committed source identity, and an unsupported premise stays a diagnostic or a charge refusal.
The breakdown preflight lists each uncited coverage row, and the rows-owned check still refuses an uncited row.
The delivery closes no roadmap row, and FT293 keeps the closure members that the staged spec does not name.
The anchor registry admits only Forbid, label, route, invariant, and command rows, and a test refuses an unclassified Require row.
The retained-workflow check and the hand-coded prose pins hold no anchor fact that the registry also holds.
The registry pins the key clause of invariants 1, 2, and 3 in .bench/BENCH.md.
ADR 0012 states the admission rule, and the guidance no longer asks for rule-sentence anchors.
bench preflight build reports a drift row for each fenced path that changed from the spec's pinned commit to the source tip, a cited-symbol row, and a cited-test row.

The build dispatches no staleness pass when every required supported row is green and the drift row is empty, and otherwise the manual pass audits only the drift, the red rows, and the unsupported claims.
The delivery closes no roadmap row, and FT375 keeps the faces that the staged spec does not name.
Preflight no longer predicts ownership closure, and the propose-writes, breakdown, and premise forms and their repeated guidance are gone.
One plan verb adds a gate-found path to a ticket's expected writes, and a path outside the approved scope goes to the reviewer.
The spec scope derives from the tickets, and the landing still refuses a path outside that scope.
The degraded Git guard refuses a malformed command, such as a joined word or an unclosed quote, before it classifies the command.
The guidance requires bench commit --preflight-build <slug> for each plan commit before the next dispatch. FT445 supersedes this rule with one build preflight for each dispatch.
A plan commit after a chunk freeze joins the review delta of the successor chunk.
The build preflight checks the chunk table against the coverage map, and a red check-floor row blocks the next charge and the review charge.
The delivery closes no roadmap row, and the check before publication and the commit-lane floor stay open on FT380.

The guidance states that any source change after a chunk freeze moves the chunk tip and needs a refreeze, and that the successor base is the last recorded source tip of its predecessor, never a record commit.
A bench worktree merge from the primary checkout grades the composed tree with the target's declared lane.
A build that adds a persisted ledger or review-record field writes and lands through a binary that reads that field.
The guards share one command projection and one set of envelope facts.
The guard inventory scan runs as one synchronous loop.
bench test reports the slowest tests of each package and the package elapsed time.
bench test warns when the elapsed time of a package nears the go test timeout that the gate uses.
The landing gate spends less time, and each changed test keeps its purpose and its failure detection.
A timing gain inside the recorded run-to-run spread counts as no change, and the build records each reverted attempt.
The build measures its timing targets again on the tmpfs base before it starts.
The delivery closes no roadmap row, and FT402 keeps the shard, git-query cache, and serial-test faces that the staged spec does not name.
One subprocess owner runs each process-group child, and the profile claim matches the tree.
Each ticket's verification entries bind to its own commit, so a later ticket's commit or a repair makes no other ticket restage.
A test-only repair whose delta adds only a completion-plan assignment block closes through bench record confirmation with no confirming round; every other plan change still takes one.
Each repair writes one plan commit, the check floor grades each chunk once, and each dispatch runs one build preflight.
The checkpoint gate starts when a chunk freezes or a repair commits, and the chunk checkpoint reuses that green when only the record changed.
A test-only delta after a whole green at the reviewed tip takes a delta checkpoint, and the landing gate always runs whole.
Exec calls of Bench commands reuse a fresh worktree binary when the measurement shows a net saving.
One census derives the checks and packages that read each non-Go path, and a check that binds a catch-all input sends its paths to the whole gate.
A landing whose every changed path is inside the census and is not a Go file runs only the reduced set, and any other landing runs the whole gate.
A periodic fresh run grades the whole gate, and a reduced green never authorizes another subject.
An unchanged landing composition reuses gate evidence only under the complete authorization key, and any key change runs the full gate.

One grade key, separate from authorization, names the tree minus the declared evidence paths, the run-binary digest, the toolchain, the schedule, and the capability posture, and each verb looks up a grade before it checks its own conditions.

The grade key builds on the FT445 chunk key without the review record and on the delta green. Since FT335 a merge runs the lane, so the spec measures the saving of the key on checkpoint-then-landing compositions and retries before any code change.
Ready landing sources compose in order and grade once as one stack, and each source keeps its own spec transition.
A red stack bisects with whole gates, and the red is attributed to one source.
A repair entry reruns each requirement that the changed-package selector reaches from the repair delta and carries each other requirement forward.
A chunk checkpoint or a landing of a lane-passed tip finds the background verdict of that tip under its grade key and runs no second gate for it.
Background grades run inside a decided machine bound measured at -p=2, and the grade of a superseded tip takes no new test slot.
Before the spec sets any slicing target, it measures the graph depth and the serial checkpoints of recent builds from git and the trace store.
Each spec retro carries a derived cost section, and a budget overrun makes the drain propose one removal or one merge without a red gate.
A ticket author pays fewer fixed record calls than the 24.5 that FT451 measured, and no recorded author run repeats a check that the checkpoint grades.
The build keeps every gate, lane pass, chunk checkpoint grade, witness red, probe, review, done-claim check, fresh author session, fresh repair session, and reviewer stop.
Before any code change, a measurement on the tmpfs base at -p=2 compares the internal/worktree package time with a per-command cache of pure git queries against the recorded run-to-run spread.
When the measured gain falls outside the spread, a command run caches its pure git queries; otherwise the outcome closes with the recorded measurement and no code change.
gittest exports one git runner and one commit identity, and the tests that pasted their own use them.

Each row of the 2026-10-09 test-efficiency review tables whose probe proves a kept test red on the same mutation is cut, and a whole-test cut in internal/worktree repins its top-level test count in the same ticket.
Before each cut, a probe proves that the subsuming test turns red on the same mutation.
Authored Markdown has one line reader for fences, frontmatter, comments, and sections.
The section, story, symbol, and worktree readers return precise slices under the output budget.
Before the first chunk, the build preflight grades each spec decision map's Sources: against the published tree.
The build-entry staleness pass takes a writes-resolve red whose every named path a landed commit deleted, if that check survives FT293-closure-removal.

An approved plan that carries a pinned row's new identity, together with the row edit, records the decision in one plan and one commit, and a pinned-row edit with no exact approved plan still refuses.
Every rebuild remedy for a pool worktree names bench worktree build from one owner.
A comment-only correction after a chunk freeze keeps its verifications and its review chain.
Every strict JSON read goes through the one jsonfile owner.
A commit in a build worktree leaves no stale dist/bench for the next preflight or --in verb.
A PreToolUse guard refuses a pathless rg call through the shared command projection.

A plan commit that no dispatch follows runs the coverage parser, the build preflight, and the check-floor row before it publishes. A plan commit that a dispatch follows takes its build preflight from the charge preparation (FT445).
The clean modes share one member-set applier.
Shell quoting has one owner, and every caller quotes through it.
Production test seams have one decided policy that the injected-port audit enforces.
A retired cache store leaves with its cache, and inherited registration has one owner.
The record, commit, and landing verbs state their preconditions before an attempt.
The delegate charge and the slicing checks close the fence and venue gaps that the row records.
Conformance tests derive restated tables from their owners and share one Go-rule scanner.
A Bench verb reaches a worktree only through --in: exec refuses a Bench child, and directory inference ends.
The review record and the author charge support the concurrent chunks of a delegated full run, and the run dispatches every eligible ticket up to the author limit.
A verified harness path preserves complete tool output before it returns a bounded replacement.
